name: Object-Centric OLAP
author: István Koren
description: The four multi-dimensional operations on an object-centric event log: drill down and roll up along the object-type dimension, unfold and fold along the event-type dimension. Each produces a new OCEL — the same log seen at a different granularity — so every discovery, view and metric in the workspace can be run again on it and the two compared. This is how an object-centric log is analysed the way a cube is: not by filtering it down, but by changing what counts as a type.

actions.label: Drill down an object type
actions.description: Splits one object type into finer sub-types named after an attribute's values: Order becomes (Order, gold) and (Order, standard). Objects whose attribute has no value keep the parent type, so nothing is placed in a category the data never claimed — and rolling up afterwards gives back exactly the log you started from.

agent.whenToUse: To ask whether a process differs by a property of the objects it handles — priority, region, customer segment — without writing a filter per value.
agent.notFor: Filtering. Nothing is removed: the log keeps every event, object and relation, and only the type names change.

objectType.title: Object type
objectType.description: The type to split. Every other type is left alone.

optionsFrom.sql: SELECT object_type AS value, COUNT(*) AS n FROM {object} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC

attribute.title: Attribute
attribute.description: The object attribute whose values name the sub-types. A time-dependent attribute is read at its earliest recorded value — an object cannot be of two types at once.

optionsFrom.sql: SELECT name AS value, COUNT(DISTINCT object_id) AS n FROM {object_attr} WHERE value IS NOT NULL AND value <> '' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC

actions.label: Roll up an object type
actions.description: Collapses the sub-types of one object type back into it: (Order, gold) and (Order, standard) become Order again. The inverse of drilling down, and inverse exactly — a drilled log rolled up on the same type is the log it was drilled from.

objectType.title: Parent type
objectType.description: The type to collapse into. Every sub-type written as “(this type, …)” is rolled back up; anything else is left alone.

optionsFrom.sql: SELECT DISTINCT regexp_extract(object_type, '^\((.*?), ', 1) AS value, COUNT(*) AS n FROM {object} WHERE object_type LIKE '(%, %)' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC

actions.label: Unfold an event type
actions.description: Splits one activity by the kind of object it touches: “pay” performed on a Customer becomes (pay, Customer), while the same activity with no such object keeps its name. That separation is what stops a model from merging two genuinely different pieces of work into one node.

agent.whenToUse: When one activity name covers work on different kinds of object, and a discovered model merges them into a node that means two things.

optionsFrom.sql: SELECT activity AS value, COUNT(*) AS n FROM {event} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC

objectType.title: Object type
objectType.description: The kind of object that names the new event type.

optionsFrom.sql: SELECT object_type AS value, COUNT(*) AS n FROM {object} GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC

qualifier.title: Only this relation
qualifier.description: Restricts which event-to-object relations count — “the customer it was paid for”, rather than any customer mentioned. Leave empty for any relation.

optionsFrom.sql: SELECT qualifier AS value, COUNT(*) AS n FROM {e2o} WHERE qualifier IS NOT NULL AND qualifier <> '' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC

actions.label: Fold an event type
actions.description: Collapses the unfolded variants of one activity back into it: (pay, Customer) and (pay, Supplier) become pay again. The inverse of unfolding, and inverse exactly.

activity.title: Parent activity
activity.description: The activity to collapse into. Every variant written as “(this activity, …)” is folded back; anything else is left alone.

optionsFrom.sql: SELECT DISTINCT regexp_extract(activity, '^\((.*?), ', 1) AS value, COUNT(*) AS n FROM {event} WHERE activity LIKE '(%, %)' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY n DESC

authors.name: István Koren
authors.affiliation: ELTE University Budapest, Data Science and Engineering

citation.text: Khayatbashi, S., Miri, N. and Jalali, A. (2025). Advancing Object-Centric Process Mining with Multi-Dimensional Data Operations. CAiSE Forum 2025 (arXiv:2412.00393). The four operations — drill down, roll up, unfold, fold — are the paper's, implemented as relational programs over the host's OCEL schema.
